provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The colour roles are fixed as constants: background is palette[0], the box outline is palette[1], and the fill/ray colour is palette[8]. The emitted program works directly in the grid as it is shown.

1. It finds each 4-connected component of the box colour and takes its bounding box. The generator's 1-cell overlap margin means each box is its own component. A gap is never at or next to a corner, so a gapped outline is still connected.
2. It fills every background cell strictly inside the bounding box with the fill colour.
3. It looks at the non-corner cells of the outline. Any background cell there is a gap, and it starts a ray. The ray goes up from the top side, down from the bottom side, left from the left side and right from the right side. It paints background cells until it reaches the grid edge or a non-background input cell.

"Away from the box, perpendicular to the gapped side" means the same thing under every rotation and reflection. So the same coordinate code is correct for all eight D4 orientations, with no inverse transform: a vertical ray in the native frame is simply detected as a horizontal gap on a left or right side in the visible frame. The generator rejects scenes where a ray would hit an interior, another ray or a box, or pass right next to a box. Under that constraint, the obstacle stop never triggers on generated data and the processing order does not matter.
draft_notes.limitations: Background, box and fill colours are fixed from the palette and are not inferred from the demonstrations. The program relies on the generator's guarantees: boxes are separate components, there is at most one gap per box and it is never on a corner, and rays never cross. Components with a bounding box thinner than 3 are skipped, as in the archived solver. The fixtures agree with this uniform rule. I have not run any tests.
